not a patient at this GP myself, but I regularly take my mum here, so I’ve seen first-hand how badly things are run and how stressful it’s been for her. Honestly, this GP surgery has been nothing but disappointing and unhelpful.

Getting an appointment is almost impossible. Even if you call exactly at 8am, you’ll be stuck on hold for 20–30 minutes, and by the time someone answers, all the appointments are already gone. The only chance to be seen is to physically go to the surgery at 8am and hope you’re one of the first few people in line. It’s incredibly unfair, especially for elderly or unwell patients who can’t stand outside waiting.

The reception staff are often rude, dismissive, and seem completely uninterested in helping. They give out mixed or incorrect information and act as though patients are inconveniencing them just by asking for an appointment. It’s unprofessional and extremely frustrating to deal with.

Most of the time, appointments are over the phone, and face-to-face visits are rare. For phone consultations, they’ll tell you the doctor could call anytime between 8am and 6pm, meaning my mum has to sit at home all day waiting, unable to go anywhere in case she misses the call. When she finally gets a face-to-face appointment, she’s told she only has 10 minutes and can talk about one issue only — even though she’s dealing with several ongoing health problems.

The overall care is poor. Many of the doctors seem distracted, rushed, and uninterested in actually helping. Even their main, so-called “top” doctors are like this — anyone who goes to this GP regularly will know exactly who I mean. Some clearly rely on Google instead of using their own medical knowledge. I’ve even witnessed one of them chatting about unrelated things during an appointment, which shows how unprofessional and disorganised the place has become.

One experience that really stood out was when my mum needed a walking stick for her ankle and back pain. The GP referred her to physiotherapy, who confirmed she needed one but said only the GP could provide it. When we went back, the GP said the opposite — that only physio could give it. We were sent back and forth four times. It was only when another external team (not connected to the GP) stepped in that my mum finally received the walking stick — with no problems at all.
To make things worse, I was once contacted by the head or manager of the GP, and instead of offering support or understanding, she told me, “We have 700 patients — we can’t look after all of them.” She spoke as if she wasn’t being paid to do her job, like helping patients was some kind of favour. Whether it’s 700 or 800 patients, that’s literally her responsibility. Hearing that from someone in charge was shocking and really showed how careless the leadership is.

This surgery has caused my mum more stress than relief. They don’t take patients’ health seriously, they pass people around, and they fail to communicate properly. Watching my mum struggle to get even basic support has been heartbreaking.

My advice: if you or a loved one have ongoing health issues, please think carefully before coming here. Try to move to another GP practice or go private if possible. This surgery desperately needs better management, proper training for staff, and doctors who genuinely care about their patients.
